TOR.head: The Maple Leafs have a hill to climb
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Somebody warn Sergei Bobrovsky
paras: The Maple Leafs (8-7-2) lost 3-2 to Utah on Tuesday, while the Devils have won three straight. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (19th).

The Devils have played better than their record (.688) says: their chances are worth about .745, and their goaltending has held them back. The Maple Leafs’ record (.529) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.478), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Devils keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), rarely throw hits (3rd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). On the other side, the Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (31st) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Devils are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Jack Hughes (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 16 GP) is carrying the Devils’ offense, with nine points in his last five games and six goals in seven games against Toronto since 2023-24. Jesper Bratt (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 16 GP) is next in line. Auston Matthews (11 G / 15 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and seven goals in eight games against New Jersey since 2023-24. William Nylander (10 G / 11 A / 21 P in 17 GP) is next in line.
Connor Hellebuyck (4-0-0 / .891 SV% in 4 GS) will likely start for New Jersey, and Sergei Bobrovsky (3-6-2 / .889 SV% in 11 GS) for Toronto.
The Devils usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko, have been without Nick Blankenburg and John Tavares for several games, and have had to make do without Max Domi all season.
Luke Hughes has six goals on chances worth about 2.1 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
